clue.text: Linen's for a nightcap, perhaps

definitions.meaning: holland is a plain-woven linen fabric, so 'Linen's' reads as ..., the possessive spelt without its apostrophe
Dutch gin, a drink one might take at bedtime

explanation.surface: Someone recommends linen bedwear, such as a nightcap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nightcap' suggests a cloth cap for bed, which fits the linen, but here it is a late-night drink; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Holland is a linen cloth, and Hollands is a Dutch gin that might serve as a bedtime drink.

clue.text: Baker Street landlady in river

definitions.meaning: Mrs ... keeps the house at 221B Baker Street where Sherlock Holmes lodges
the river flowing through New York State into New York Harbour

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes's landlady goes for a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes's housekeeper in Conan Doyle's stories shares a surname with the great New York waterway.

clue.text: See fit to meet an American poet

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
well means fit, healthy

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it right to meet a poet from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See fit' reads as one phrase meaning think proper; it is two pieces, LO and WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Lowell and James Russell Lowell were both notable US writers of verse.

clue.text: Such voices prophesied war in Xanadu

definitions.text: Such voices prophesied war in Xanadu

parts.words: Such voices prophesied war in Xanadu
parts.note: Coleridge's Kubla Khan, set in Xanadu, has the line about voices from forefathers prophesying war

explanation.surface: A line about warnings heard in Kubla Khan's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's poem reads 'And 'mid this tumult Kubla heard from far / Ancestral voices prophesying war!'
explanation.definitionFit: The voices in the poem belong to Kubla's forefathers, so they are of his lineage.

clue.text: Sad part of midnight gramophone recital ?

definitions.meaning: read as four words, the phrase says a record is on at such a late hour

explanation.surface: A lonely person plays records into the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into DISC ON SO LATE, what someone playing a gramophone at midnight might hear complained of.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot be comforted is utterly dejected; split up, the word describes a record still playing late at night.

clue.text: See head man to get a move?

definitions.meaning: a see is a ... diocese, so its head is the ...
the chess piece of that name moves diagonally across the board

explanation.surface: Someone is told to visit the boss to secure a transfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the verb 'visit', but it is a noun: a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocesan prelate heads a see, and the chessman of the same name makes diagonal moves.

clue.text: Fashionable tax, but altogether fatuous

parts.note: in means fashionable
EPT was Excess Profits Tax, a British wartime levy

explanation.surface: A trendy levy that is wholly foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: EPT, Excess Profits Tax, was a tax on businesses in Britain during the World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means foolish or clumsy, lacking sense.

clue.text: Keats's Derby winner

definitions.meaning: Keats wrote an unfinished epic poem about the Titan sun god
the racehorse of that name won the Derby in 1933

explanation.surface: A racehorse belonging to the poet Keats wins at Epsom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's premier flat horse race, at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's epic about a Titan shares its title with a famous Epsom-winning colt.

clue.text: It's agreeable to have money in rustic surroundings

indicators.note: the rustic word encloses the money word within it

parts.note: a peasant is a country labourer, a rustic
L stands for pounds, from Latin librae

explanation.surface: It's nice to have cash when living in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rustic' looks like an adjective for the surroundings; it is the noun, a countryman, and 'surroundings' puts L inside PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasant is enjoyable or nice.

clue.text: Dejected Ulster players, perhaps

parts.note: Down is one of the six counties of Ulster, in Northern Ireland
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: An Ulster team, perhaps, is downhearted after a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals that Down is just one example of an Ulster county.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone downcast is low in spirits, a synonym of dejected.

clue.text: Side-face view of archbishop

definitions.meaning: the flat part at the side of the head, between eye and ear
William ... and his father Frederick were both Archbishops of Canterbury

explanation.surface: A profile portrait of a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side-face view' reads as a profile picture of the archbishop; 'view of' is only a link joining two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The temple is part of the face seen side-on, and Temple was the surname of two Canterbury primates.

clue.text: Recording distribution of tigers' food, perhaps

indicators.note: the letters of tigers are dealt out into a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter
a ration is an allowance of food

explanation.surface: Someone logs how the zoo's tigers have their meals shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution of' rearranges TIGERS into REGIST; 'perhaps' marks food as one kind of ration.
explanation.definitionFit: Registration is the act of entering details in an official list, a form of recording.

clue.text: Looks like Casanova, perhaps

parts.note: not resembling the great lover but staring at women amorously, as such a seducer would

explanation.surface: Someone resembles the famous Venetian seducer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks like' seems to mean resembles; it is the verb 'looks' in the manner of a womaniser, gazing with desire.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer at someone with amorous intent is a lustful glance of the kind a seducer gives.

clue.text: Proposals put before people of 21

definitions.meaning: offers or approaches made to open negotiations
pieces of music played at the start by the band of 21-across

explanation.surface: Suggestions are laid before a group of 21-year-olds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people of 21' reads as twenty-one-year-olds, but 21 is the clue number of ORCHESTRA; its players perform the opening pieces before an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening offers in a negotiation share a name with the instrumental pieces that precede an opera.

clue.text: Nurse's application to high place brings reprimand

parts.note: a nurse applies a dressing to a wound
a down is an area of open upland, as in the South Downs of England

explanation.surface: A nurse applies to work somewhere senior and is rebuked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' suggests a job application; it is the bandage a nurse puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down is a severe scolding, a stern telling-off.

clue.text: An examination with a crib? Good heavens!

parts.note: Greats is the final honours examination in classics at Oxford
a cot is a child's bed, a crib

explanation.surface: Surprise at a student cheating in an exam with a crib sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crib' suggests cheating notes; it is a baby's bed. Greats is the Oxford classics degree exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Scott! is an old exclamation of surprise, like Good heavens!

clue.text: Attended to creeds in Reformation

indicators.note: re-formation, the letters of the words are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone saw to the church's creeds during the Reformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attended to' reads as one phrase, but 'to' belongs to the fodder; the Reformation era is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to accompany them, so escorted means attended.

clue.text: Wretched child takes Bill in both ways at cards

indicators.note: the child word takes the bill letters inside it

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved child
AC, short for account, a bill, written forwards and then backwards

explanation.surface: A naughty child pockets a banknote at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in both ways' gives AC then CA, ACCA, which sits inside BRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game, the one played by James Bond.

clue.text: Little habit of a gentleman in Nicholas Nickleby

definitions.text: of a gentleman in Nicholas Nickleby
definitions.meaning: Mrs Nickleby's eccentric neighbour is called the old gentleman in ...

explanation.surface: A minor quirk of one of Dickens's characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' looks like a custom or quirk; it is dress, as in a monk's habit. Smallclothes were close-fitting knee breeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Knee breeches were called small clothes, and Dickens names the mad neighbour by that garment.

clue.text: First male artist to turn up in the fleet

indicators.note: in a down light the joined words are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: The first man and an artist appear among the warships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses ADAMRA as a whole to give ARMADA.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a great fleet of warships, like the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Girl appears pleased ? Yes, being heartless

parts.note: glad means pleased

indicators.note: the word yes loses its central letter

explanation.surface: A girl looks happy and says yes, though she is cold at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being heartless' removes the middle E from YES to give YS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a female first name.

clue.text: Where once the chorus rather than the players performed

definitions.text: Where once the chorus rather than the players performed

parts.words: Where once the chorus rather than the players performed
parts.note: in ancient Greek theatre the circular dancing floor before the stage was the chorus's space

explanation.surface: A historical note on staging, where singers took the floor instead of the instrumentalists.
explanation.walkthrough: In a modern theatre the word names the instrumentalists, the 'players'; in the Greek theatre it was the space where the chorus danced and sang, while actors used the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word meant a dancing place, the semicircle in front of the stage used by the chorus.

clue.text: Like the essayist's work, shows some self-reliance

indicators.note: only part of the word is displayed, the run of letters within self-reliance

explanation.surface: The essays display a certain independence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the essayist' is Charles Lamb, who wrote as Elia; the run is inside 'reliance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elian means relating to Elia, the pen name of Charles Lamb, so it describes his essays.

clue.text: A novice has his plate in Austria

definitions.note: the clue names a place within Austria; the answer is a region there

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner
a novice driver displays an L-plate, for Learner

explanation.surface: A beginner brings his own dish while staying in Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate' looks like crockery; it is the L-plate a learner driver must show in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tirol is an Alpine state of western Austria, a region of that country.

clue.text: Artisan doesn't finish repairing wood-inlay

indicators.note: re-pairing, the remaining letters are matched up anew in a fresh order
the word Artisan stops short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A craftsman leaves his mending of inlaid woodwork incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't finish' drops the last letter of ARTISAN to leave ARTISA; 'repairing' then rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsia is intarsia, decorative inlaid work in wood, a marquetry technique.

clue.text: Fish, back cut, supplied by firm

indicators.note: the word for cut is read from end to start

parts.note: to clip is to cut
hard means firm, solid

explanation.surface: A fish, its back cut off, is delivered by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CLIP to give PILC. 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilchard is a small oily sea fish related to the herring, an adult sardine.

clue.text: Animal can come inside-fond of it

indicators.note: the can word enters within the animal word

parts.note: a dog is an animal
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A pet can be let indoors and is attached to the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like the verb 'is able to'; it is a container, put inside DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means showing excessive affection, being foolishly devoted.

clue.text: Ernie's make-up

parts.note: ERNIE, the premium bond number picker, is named by the first letters of Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment

explanation.surface: Someone called Ernie puts on cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' suggests cosmetics but means composition: ERNIE in Britain picks Premium Bond winners, and its name is formed from the first letters of the words in its full title.
explanation.definitionFit: An acronym such as this machine's name is built from the leading letters of words.
